digest.component_or_area: CI lint enforcement for canonical store write seams
propositions: Production bugs (3435, 3a33, 4dd2, 4c6c) resulted from store write paths that bypassed canonical write seams via raw git add/commit/rm commands, including in GitHub workflow YAML.

A two-layer deterministic CI lint must flag raw git mutations in Python (AST-based, module-agnostic) and in workflows/shell (cwd-aware within tracker context), with sanction via mandatory inline marker.

Python layer (R1/R2) detects raw subprocess invocations with git mutation verbs (add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean) and calls to shared git wrappers (run_git, run_git_write, _run_git, _git) via intra-function local variable tracking; opaque argv resolves fail-closed.

Workflow/shell layer flags git mutations only when the same step/script establishes tracker context (cd into .tickets-tracker, git -C <tracker-path>, or working-directory: naming it), excluding ordinary non-tracker repo commits.

Every report-mode bootstrap hit must be remediated or marked with an inline # raw-git-ok: <reason> comment; marker without reason fails the lint; accepted residual includes cross-function and dynamically computed argv construction.

Teaching message directs authors to the sanctioned write APIs (rebar.tickets, _store.event_append, _commands.txn) and reconciler git_adapter; docs clarify the distinction between the new raw-git-ok marker and the existing tickets-boundary-ok convention.
